There is one panda attraction within 5 km of the monument, and it is about 4.1 km away on foot.

**The monument:** this is the Ángel de la Independencia (Monumento a la Independencia) on Paseo de la Reforma, Mexico City. Porfirio Díaz inaugurated it in 1910 for the centenary of Mexican independence.

**The panda attraction:** it is the "Panda Gigante" (Giant Pandas) exhibit at the Chapultepec Zoo. It is tagged in OpenStreetMap as a giant panda attraction (*Ailuropoda melanoleuca*) at 19.4222, -99.1892.

**Walking distance:** the route is about **4.1 km**, roughly 50 to 55 minutes at a normal walking pace. The routing tool's own duration figures looked like driving speeds, so that time is my estimate from the distance. The route goes:
1. From the monument along Av. Río Tíber (about 0.7 km).
2. Along Av. Ejército Nacional Oriente and Calle Gutenberg (about 0.9 km).
3. Across Calzada Mariano Escobedo and along Calle Rubén Darío (about 1.1 km).
4. Along Calzada Chivatito and Av. Heroico Colegio Militar into Chapultepec Park and the zoo (about 0.8 km).

**Limits of this answer:**
- The OpenStreetMap search found no other panda-tagged attractions in the 5 km radius, such as panda-themed museums or exhibits.
- The web search was blocked, so I couldn't check whether the zoo's pandas are currently on display. The zoo's giant panda population has declined over the years, so check the zoo's official site before visiting.
- This is the distance to the panda exhibit's mapped point. The path inside the zoo to the exhibit adds some distance beyond the route above.

**Park:** Abraham Lincoln Birthplace National Historical Park, at 2995 Lincoln Farm Road, Hodgenville, KY 42748. The Birthplace Unit is about 2 miles south of Hodgenville on US 31E. The Knob Creek boyhood home unit is about 10 miles northeast. The NPS lists guided tours, wildlife watching and birdwatching. Its coordinates are 37.5859, -85.6733.

**Oldest painting of Lincoln:** I couldn't verify this one. The searches kept returning the same unrelated results. My page fetch also returned the wrong page. The best-supported candidate I found is George Peter Alexander Healy's *Abraham Lincoln* (1860, oil on canvas), now in the National Gallery of Art. It was commissioned in 1860 and is inscribed "G.P.A Healy / 1860". That only shows it is an early portrait. It doesn't show it is the oldest, and other 1860 portraits, such as Thomas Hicks's, may predate it. I'd check the Lincoln Presidential Library or the National Portrait Gallery before relying on it.

Sources:
- [National Gallery of Art: Healy, Abraham Lincoln](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/166453-abraham-lincoln)
- [NPS: Abraham Lincoln Birthplace NHP](https://www.nps.gov/abli/index.htm)
